To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the ob/ob mouse aorta, insulin-induced Akt/eNOS activation and endothelium-dependent relaxation are negatively regulated by GRK2, which may translocate from the cytosol to membranes upon insulin stimulation and may interact with β-arrestin-2.
in the aorta of ob/ob mouse, GRK2, in a negative regulatory manner, controls insulin-induced Akt/ eNOS signaling, in part, by regulating β-arrestin2.

in aortas isolated from ob/ob (diabetic) mice: 1) GRK2, upon translocation to membrane, is a key negative regulator for the insulin-induced Akt/eNOS pathway and for endothelium-dependent vasorelaxation; 2) GRK2 may regulate the β-arrestins, which, in turn, modulate the insulin-induced Akt signaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of GRK2 in insulin-induced Akt/eNOS pathway signaling.
the role of GRK2 and its interaction with β-arrestin in the regulation of endothelial function and vascular homeostasis.
a new mechanism for insulin-induced endothelial dysfunction in type 2 diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in aortas of ob/ob mice, GRK2 and, to a lesser degree, β-arrestins 1 and 2 are important negative modulators of insulin-induced Akt/ eNOS signaling, and that the impaired insulin-induced relaxation in ob/ob aorta may be due to the GRK2/β-arrestin 1/2–mediated negative modulation of the insulin-induced Akt/eNOS pathway.

GRK2 and/or β-arrestin2 are involved in the regulation of the insulin responsiveness in the aortic endothelial cells, and that this regulation is important in the development of the diabetic endothelial dysfunction.
GRK2 and its interacting protein, β-arrestins, are important negative regulators of insulin signaling in aorta of diabetic mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in ob/ob mice, GRK2 is a key negative regulator in the insulin-induced Akt/eNOS pathway in the endothelium.
GRK2 and/or β-arrestin are potential therapeutic targets in type 2 diabetes.
GRK2 is a key regulator of insulin-induced endothelium-dependent relaxation in mouse aorta.
The main takeaway from our work is that

GRK2 and, possibly, β-arrestins, may be key regulators of the insulin responsiveness of the vascular relaxation response and that their dysregulation may contribute to diabetic endothelial dysfunction.
the GRK2/β-arrestin 1/2/Akt/eNOs pathway may play a role in diabetic endothelial dysfunctions.
GRK2, with β-arrestin, is a key mediator of insulin-induced Akt/eNOS activation in mouse aorta.
